dedupe_keys.name: annual irrigated cropland mapping reveals uneven expansion and rising water demand in africa from 2000 to 2021

description: Misgana Abera Tolera and colleagues publish annual irrigated-cropland maps for Africa from 2000 to 2021. The 2026 Zenodo release provides a ZIP and README under CC BY 4.0, with free access. The documentation describes binary irrigated and non-irrigated rasters at approximately 500 metres, represented as 0.00449-degree cells in EPSG:4326. These maps can define spatial irrigation extent when estimating crop-water demand, locating supply needs or constructing agricultural transformation scenarios. They classify land use, not measure actual withdrawals or irrigation-system capacity. The provider reports validation against 5,874 points and approximately eighty percent overall accuracy; neither the validation sample nor spatial error patterns were independently checked. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this annual Africa-wide product. Classification uncertainty and coarse pixels can affect local demand estimates. Raster values were not downloaded or compared with other inventories.
